method_specification.framework_is_gp2sca.reason: Both yes-criteria components are present. (1) The full-scale run performs a gp2Scale-style sparse distributed assembly of the 500,112x500,112 covariance: a Dask LocalCluster with 8 requested workers (5 registered addresses logged) returns 15 sparse temporal-row blocks that are stacked to CSR (nnz 70,024,328). fvGP's sparse CG solve (relative residual 7.9e-9) and SLQ log-det run on that matrix. (2) Hyperparameters are sampled by block Metropolis-Hastings (3 blocks, 60 proposals) after a Nelder-Mead initialization. The caveat is that each NM/BMH likelihood evaluation uses an exact Kronecker eigendecomposition of the separable factors, not the assembled sparse matrix; the sparse path serves as the production solve and audit at the selected state. This shortcut is exact (same covariance, all observations, log-det and quadratic form exact) and is documented and justified in Section 2.3. It is cross-checked against the sparse solution (relative difference 1.2e-8), so the work stays within the exact-GP-at-scale paradigm rather than substituting an approximate scalable method. Confidence is medium because training scalability comes from grid separability rather than from exploiting sparsity.

method_specification.kernel_adaptation_s.reason: The paper gives the full mathematics. W(u) is Eq. 3. K_G(rho)=D^{-1/2} B B^T D^{-1/2}, with B=I+rho*A and A row-normalized after keeping the two strongest outgoing DCRNN links (Eq. 5). K_T has a local Wendland term plus eta*1{same phase, P=288}*W(|d(t)-d(t')|/r_d) with r_d=8 (Eqs. 6-7). The product kernel is Eq. 8, with a PSD argument and five learned parameters. These match code/traffic_kernels.py exactly, so the kernel can be reimplemented from the paper plus the cited DCRNN adjacency. The motivation is domain-structural: directed carriageways and downstream coupling, plus same-clock-phase daily recurrence that a stationary compact taper cannot reach sparsely.

kernel_contribution.kernel_differs_from_.reason: DIR multiplies two factors. The first is a diagonally normalized Gram of directed one-hop road-incidence features (I + rho*A_top2), a learned graph kernel whose zeros follow network incidence rather than any Euclidean radius. The second is a temporal kernel that adds local Wendland support to a compact same-phase daily-recurrence term on the day quotient. It is implemented in code and used in the full-scale run. It is algebraically related to the paper's feature-product and delta masks (sum_p g_p(x_i) g_p(x_j); 'parametric delta positions' in Section 4.4). However, the directed-incidence feature map with a learned propagation weight and normalization, and the quotient-time recurrence, go meaningfully beyond the published Wendland, non-stationary Wendland, bump and delta kernels. It is not a bandwidth re-tune.

kernel_contribution.existing_kernel_inad.reason: The paper's stationary Wendland kernel was run on the domain at full scale with the same optimization budget and test set. RMSE is essentially tied (5.416 vs DIR 5.396), but CRPS is much worse (4.960 vs 2.889) and calibration is overdispersed (95% coverage 99.78%; mean absolute calibration error 19.72 vs 5.77 percentage points). The structural sweep at N=500,112 shows that stationary support long enough to capture daily recurrence is infeasible: 5 km x 1 day needs 10,158,379,600 nnz (about 121.9 GB, more than the 66.32 GB RAM), and 0.5 km x 1 day exceeds the 5e8 cap. Two caveats: only one paper kernel was tested, and both kernels' optimizers were unconverged.

kernel_contribution.adaptation_motivated.reason: The construction is justified from the domain's correlation and sparsity structure. Adjacent detectors can sit on disconnected carriageways while interchange-separated sensors share downstream congestion, which motivates the directed-incidence spatial factor. Speeds recur at the same clock phase on nearby days, which motivates the quotient-time recurrence; a stationary compact taper would need day-wide dense support to capture it. The plan's inadequacy hypothesis states both failure modes in advance.

kernel_contribution.domain_warrants_new_.reason: Traffic speed on a directed freeway network has non-Euclidean (directed graph) spatial dependence and non-stationary, daily-periodic temporal dependence. The submission shows that, under gp2Scale's explicit sparse-assembly constraint, kernel choice governs feasibility: stationary Euclidean support reaching daily recurrence would need about 1e10 covariance entries. The stock kernel is also markedly worse in CRPS and calibration. Two caveats keep confidence at medium: on a complete sensor-by-time grid any separable kernel is tractable through Kronecker algebra, and the graph component's benefit was empirically null (Spearman -0.017). So the case is weaker than a chemistry or biology domain, but the domain is not trivially Euclidean or stationary.
evidence: proposal/logs/analysis.json wendland_support_density_sweep (5 km x 288 frames: 10,158,379,600 nnz, 121.9 GB)

insight_contribution.insight_present.reason: The paper states a non-trivial domain and method insight beyond 'it beat the baseline'. Daily phase recurrence mainly changes the scale and calibration of multi-hour forecasts rather than the mean, so RMSE-only traffic benchmarks would pick Vecchia and treat DIR and Wendland as tied. It also reports a negative finding: graph-versus-Euclidean support mismatch does not explain sensor-level gains. This is more than a shallow 'uncertainty is higher in sparse regions' remark, although its causal support is limited (see the grounding node).

insight_contribution.insight_grounded_in.reason: The descriptive sub-claims trace to logged artifacts: long-horizon (150 min and beyond, n=4,036) RMSE/CRPS/coverage for all methods, learned eta=0.331 and r_l=44.7 min, the long-horizon SDs (20.26 vs 5.79 mph), the spatial-mismatch Spearman test and the sensor-717804 audit. The central causal attribution is not backed by any isolating artifact. That attribution is that recurrence 'repairs scale' and that 'DIR's sparse same-phase links maintain a posterior SD near 5.79 mph'. There is no ablation with eta=0 and no Wendland-plus-recurrence run. The logged hyperparameters point to a different proximate cause. DIR's long-horizon SD (5.79) is close to its own prior SD: sqrt(23.76*1.331+4.51)=6.01, so recurrence links reduce variance by only about 7%, and with eta=0 the prior SD would be 5.32. Wendland's 20.26 equals its prior SD, with signal variance 399.5 at the 400 upper bound. The scale gap therefore mostly reflects the learned marginal variances. The claim that normalizing K_G and homoscedastic noise suppress spatial reliability contrast is also inferred rather than tested. Some insights are supported; the key mechanism is asserted.

Its predecessor set is domain-aware: 12 own lags, directed upstream lags, same-phase previous-day values and nearest sensors. Its Matérn-3/2 x (local + daily recurrence) kernel gives it the same recurrence structure as DIR. Five hyperparameters were optimized by L-BFGS-B from three jittered starts; each converged (18-19 iterations, 132-138 evaluations) and the traces are logged. failure_analysis.patterns_explained_cohe.reason: The main explanations are principled and consistent with the evidence. Infeasibility comes from exact structural nnz counts at N=500,112. The uniform DIR uncertainty is explained by unit-diagonal normalization of K_G plus homoscedastic noise, which fits the logged 1.012 max/min SD ratio. Non-convergence is explained by the fixed 35-iteration and 60-proposal budgets, which fits the still-rising traces in Figure 2. Weak spots: attributing Vecchia's overcoverage to the lower-bound hits is poorly argued, since its long-horizon SD of about 10.1 equals its prior SD and bounded noise would narrow intervals. The Wendland signal variance sitting at its 400 bound is not discussed. These are secondary and do not make the analysis hand-waving overall.

code_paper_alignment.methodology_describ.reason: The Methodology describes what the code does. Covariance: K = sigma_f^2 (K_T kron K_G) + sigma_n^2 I with time-major vectorization. Polynomial: W(u) = (1-u)^8 (32u^3 + 25u^2 + 8u + 1) in both the paper's equation and traffic_kernels.py. The stock Wendland is applied separably, and the paper says so. Every Nelder-Mead/BMH evaluation uses the exact Kronecker eigen-likelihood on all 500,112 observations. Optimization: 35 Nelder-Mead iterations (maxiter 35, log message confirms the limit was hit), then 20 cycles of 3 blocks (60 proposals) with the stated block structure, keeping the highest-likelihood accepted state. Assembly: Dask block assembly requesting 8 workers; the paper says 'requested', and the log shows 5 registered addresses and 15/18 blocks. Solves: fvGP sparse CG and the SLQ log-determinant are called. Prediction uses the exact eigensystem. Vecchia: the described predecessor set and Matérn-3/2 recurrent kernel, with 3,539 patterns. Harmonic mean: training-only, as stated. Two points are unverifiable but not contradictory. The paper credits the 32-coefficient polynomial to fvGP; fvGP's source is not in the staged snapshot, and the paper's formula matches the submitted code. The MNIST code clips predictions to [0,1] without saying so, but I verified the clip changes nothing. No material contradiction.

baseline_honesty.baseline_genuine_best_e.reason: Vecchia: trained at the full 500,112 points with 30 predecessors (the original paper's default). Its predecessor set includes directed-upstream and previous-day same-phase neighbors, and its kernel has the same compact daily recurrence DIR uses. Three jittered initializations all converged to the same optimum (approximate LL -1,414,660.38). The noise and spatial-length lower-bound hits are disclosed in the paper and the attempts log, and Vecchia wins RMSE, which is reported. Existing-kernel Wendland: given the same initial signal and noise variance and the same 35 Nelder-Mead + 60 BMH budget as DIR. The preregistered 5e8 sparsity cap never fired (0 rejections), and the learned supports are interior to their bounds (0.585 km within [0.5, 10]; 29.38 frames within [2.1, 60]). Its signal variance did reach the shared upper bound of 400 (399.48; 6 out-of-bounds BMH proposals rejected), and the paper does not mention this. The same bound applies to all three models and was set before any run. Relaxing it would raise Wendland's already 20.26 mph prior SD, so it would not narrow DIR's CRPS or calibration advantage. Limited tuning and a shared bound are not affirmative evidence of deliberate weakening.
